Not to rain on your parade (haha, joking) but if all you have is an idea you have nothing.

There are over 7 billion people in the world with ridiculously similar thought processes - if you have "an idea" chances are there are already at least a dozen people working on getting it implemented. An even greater likelihood is that it has already been implemented and your "idea" is just viral marketing for something about to hit the market that seeped into your brain.

Learn how to implement things before trying to come up with ideas for them - to be an "idea man" you need millions of dollars in expendable cash.

You need to develop a business plan. It's a process and if done right will make you activity decide to continue, or let the plan die, numerous times. After you go threw this process, you will have developed the tools you need to convince a bank or investors to consider your idea and get you the working capital you need to start.

It can be tricky to do solo and needs carful thought and analysis at various stages. I have done a number of these and will blindly offer you a helper until I don't think it's worth pursuing. PM me and I'll get you started.

First you need to create a proof of concept. Perhaps pick a few people and give it to them for free as a testbed that you can accurately and reliably deliver product.

The information and experience you will get from filling 10 orders a week for a month will dwarf the revenue you will lose for doing it for free.

Then work out where you will be best at delivering it. (Are you going locally only or using online to spread out)
